news.title: Report 2026 05 Supply Chain Risks
news.summary: May 2026 Supply Chain Disruption Risks: As we look toward the 2026 harvest, procurement intelligence must factor in elevated logistics and operational risks. Road freight capacity from Turkey to the EU is currently constrained by new border inspection protocols, adding 2-3 days to typical transit ti
takeaways: Furthermore, labor shortages for the upcoming harvest season in both Italy and Turkey remain a pressing concern, potentially delaying the availability of new crop materials in September.
On a positive note, the crop development looks excellent so far, with a high yield forecast mitigating some of the supply chain gloom.
Prices are currently trending upwards steadily, largely driven by these friction costs rather than raw material scarcity.

news.title: Report 2026 03 2026 Crop Outlook
news.summary: March 2026: Early signs show the 2026 crop in Turkey is recovering. Prices stabilizing.

news.title: Report 2026 01 Seasonal Buying
news.summary: January 2026 Seasonal Buying Strategy: Post-holiday inventory assessments show that European warehouses are drawn down slightly more than anticipated, leaving days-of-supply metrics at the lower end of the comfortable range. While Q1 is traditionally a slower period for raw material purchasing, the
takeaways: The Turkish Lira's volatility continues to create pricing anomalies, offering brief windows of opportunity for buyers holding EUR or USD to secure favorable terms.

We recommend a staggered buying approach: covering 60% of Q2/Q3 needs now to mitigate the risk of a Q2 rally, while leaving 40% open to capitalize on potential late-season distress sales by farmers needing cash for spring agricultural inputs.
Current Italian prices reflect a premium that may soften by March.

news.title: Report 2025 10 Global Market Update
news.summary: October 2025: With Turkey's low yield confirmed around 550K tons, Italian and US crops are heavily relied upon.

news.title: Report 2025 10 Competitive Landscape
news.summary: October 2025 Competitive Landscape: The hazelnut processing sector is undergoing rapid consolidation. This month's acquisition of two mid-sized Turkish cracking facilities by a major multinational trading house signals a shift towards tighter vertical integration.
takeaways: For large buyers, this means fewer independent suppliers and potentially reduced price competition at the origin.
However, it also promises better quality control and easier compliance with EU sustainability mandates.
In response, independent farmers are forming stronger cooperatives to negotiate better prices.

news.title: Report 2025 07 Supply Outlook Post Frost
news.summary: July 2025: The market is still reeling from the April frost. Prices remain at historic highs near 9 EUR/kg.

news.title: Report 2025 04 Turkey Frost Crisis
news.summary: CRITICAL: April 2025. Severe frost has destroyed an estimated 50% of the Turkish hazelnut crop.
takeaways: Prices have spiked dramatically by 35% across the board.
The expected 700K ton yield will likely plummet to 450K-609K tons.
We need to secure remaining stocks globally.
